reasoning_summary:
Step-by-step verification (line ranges of the numbered source; lines 0001-0116 and 0566-0593 are preamble/title/abstract/bibliography and carry no mathematical claim).

0117-0131 Definitions of d_k, mu, M(x): standard, correct.
0138-0148 P^-(n), P^-(1)=infinity, d_k'(n,y): well defined.
0149-0156 d_k^*(n,y): well defined; note for k>=2 the constraint n_i not in {1,n} is equivalent to n_i>1 (if one part equals n the rest are 1).
0157-0160 M(x,y): well defined; since y>=3 the two admitted sets (P^-(n)>y, n odd; n=2m with P^-(m)>y) are disjoint.
0165-0183 Theorem (Inversion Formula), statement: correct. beta is exactly the Dirichlet inverse of alpha: beta(n)=sum_{k>=1}(-1)^k alpha(1)^{-k-1} sum_{d_1...d_k=n, d_i>1} prod alpha(d_i); the displayed k=1 term -alpha(n)/alpha(1) has no exclusion (right), and for k>=2 the exclusion n_i!=n is vacuous, so the display agrees with the standard formula; substituting F into the claimed G gives sum_{k<=X}(beta*alpha)(k)G(X/k)=G(X). Defect of statement only: the hypothesis alpha(1)!=0 is never stated though it is used throughout; also a misplaced '&' inside the cases environment (typographical).
0185-0199 U(X), alpha(n,y): well defined.
0200-0205 Euler-product identity: verified. First factor zeta^{-1}prod_{3<=p<=y}(1-p^{-s})^{-1} is the Dirichlet series of the summand of M(x,y) (= (1-2^{-s})prod_{p>y}(1-p^{-s})); second factor zeta(s)(1-2^{-s})prod_{3<=p<=y}(1-p^{-s}) = zeta(s)prod_{p<=y}(1-p^{-s}) is the Dirichlet series of alpha(.,y); product = 1-2^{-s}.
0206-0210 U(X)=sum_{n<=X}alpha(n,y)M(X/n,y): correct, since sum_{m<=X}(f*g)(m)=sum_{n<=X}f(n)sum_{h<=X/n}g(h) and the coefficient function of 1-2^{-s} has summatory function exactly U.
0211-0215 M(X,y)=sum_{n<=X}beta(n,y)U(X/n)=sum over floor(X/2)<n<=floor(X): correct, U(X/n)=1 iff X/2<n<=X, and n>X/2 iff n>=floor(X/2)+1 in both parity cases.
0216-0219 beta(n,y)=sum_{k=1}^{Omega(n)}(-1)^k d_k^*(n,y): correct. prod_i alpha(n_i,y)=1 exactly when P^-(n)>y (divisors of a y-rough number are y-rough), so the k-th inner sum equals d_k^*(n,y); parts >1 force k<=Omega(n).
0221-0222 Truncation at log X/log y: correct, every part of an admissible factorization exceeds y, so n>y^k.
0224-0228 d_k^*=d_k'-k d_{k-1}^*-C(k,2)d_{k-2}^*-...-C(k,k-1)d_1^*: correct for n>1 (classify factorizations by the set of positions carrying a 1: d_k'=sum_{j=1}^k C(k,j)d_j^*, and C(k,k-j)=C(k,j) reconciles the displayed coefficients). FALSE at n=1: d_2'(1,y)=1, d_1^*(1,y)=1, d_2^*(1,y)=0, but the identity gives 1-2=-1. This is a literal failure, but an isolated edge case with no consequence for anything downstream.
0229-0230 F_{l,y} a linear combination of zeta^k prod_{p<=y}(1-p^{-s})^k: correct up to an additive constant produced by the n=1 discrepancy above; the constant shifts the coefficient series by O(1) and affects neither Res_{s=1} nor the order of Delta_{l,y}.
0232-0235 Definition of Delta_{l,y}: legitimate; F_{l,y} has a pole of order at most l at s=1 so the residue is defined.
0237-0257 Definition of 'level' and the consequence |M(x,y)| << x exp(-c(log x)^{a1}(log_2 x)^{a2}): the deduction from (PreobMXyId) is essentially right, since beta(n,y)=beta_{l_0}(n,y) for all n<=x (d_k^*=0 for k>log n/log y and l_0>log x/log y), so M(x,y)=sum_{n<=x}beta_{l_0}-sum_{n<=x/2}beta_{l_0}. Gap: the second sum needs the two level bounds at x/2 as well, which the definition (stated at a single x with l_0 tied to that x) does not supply. Minor uniformity gap, repairable.
0258-0267 The y_0 choice and (PreobMxyassert): explicitly hypothetical ('if l_0 were the level'), so nothing is asserted here; correct as a conditional.
0268-0270 Parenthetical claim that (PreobDeltal0yx) 'can be proved' as in [Koukoulopoulos], with the admission that the residue term (Preobresest) is 'quite complicated': an unproved assertion plus an explicit acknowledgement that the other half of the hypothesis is not established. This is where the paper's program is left open, but it is honestly flagged and Theorem PreobZF is correspondingly conditional.
0271-0284 Theorem PreobZF: stated 'with the above assumptions', i.e. conditional on the unproved level hypothesis; moreover the passage from (PreobMxyassert) to the zero-free region and PNT error term is only asserted ('one could infer, using methods of Pintz'), never carried out. Not proved here, but not claimed unconditionally either.
0287-0294 Remark that for non-principal chi there is no residue term and no logarithmic derivative: the absence of a pole at s=1 for non-principal L-functions is correct; the inference that 'strong estimates could be obtained' is unsupported speculation at this point.
0296-0310 Theorem PreobZZ: an UNCONDITIONAL, effective Landau-Siegel bound beta_0 <= 1-c/log q. Statement only; everything hinges on Section 4. The added remark (0308-0310) that the restriction chi(2)=1 can be removed is asserted without argument.
0312-0322 Lemma (Mertens): correct, (log-d)*mu = Lambda - 1 since log*mu=Lambda and d*mu=1.
0323-0327 Its proof: correct; the interchange sum_{m<=X}sum_{n|m} = sum_{n<=X}sum_{h<=X/n} is valid.
0329-0346 Lemma (M from Delta): correct specialization of Theorem 1 with alpha=log-d, alpha(1)=-1, giving 1/alpha(1)=-1 and (-alpha(1))^k=1.
0348-0358 Numerical values at X=6: all verified. psi(6)-6=2log2+log3+log5-6, psi(3)-3=log2+log3-3, psi(2)-2=log2-2, and -1 for X/4,X/5,X/6; M(6)=-1, M(3)=-1, M(2)=0, M(1.5)=M(1.2)=M(1)=1.
0359-0387 The 6x6 upper-triangular matrix: verified entry by entry against a(n)=log n-d(n) with a(1)=-1, a(2)=log2-2, a(3)=log3-2, a(4)=2log2-3, a(5)=log5-2, a(6)=log2+log3-4, and row k containing a(n) in column kn for kn<=6.
0388-0408 The solution row vector: verified by back-substitution. Coefficients (-1, 2-log2, 2-log3, -(log2)^2+2log2-1, 2-log5, -2log2log3+3log2+3log3-4) are exactly what the system yields, and they agree with b_n from Lemma 2 (b_4=-(a(4)+a(2)^2), b_6=-(a(6)+2a(2)a(3))). Correct.
0410-0429 Restatement of Theorem 1: same statement as 0165-0183; correct.
0431-0448 Setup of the triangular system F_(k)(X)=sum_{n<=X/k}alpha(n)G_(kn)(X): correct; the matrix is upper triangular with alpha(1) on the diagonal, hence nonsingular when alpha(1)!=0.
0449 Dividing every equation by -alpha(1): legitimate (requires alpha(1)!=0, unstated).
0450-0457 Cramer's-rule expression beta(n)=(-1)^{n+1}det A'_{n,1}/((-alpha(1))det A'): correct; I checked it reproduces beta(3)=-alpha(3)/alpha(1)^2 and beta(4)=-alpha(4)/alpha(1)^2+alpha(2)^2/alpha(1)^3 for floor(X)=4, matching (Preobbetanproof).
0458-0467 The row-reduction derivation: DEFECTIVE AS WRITTEN. Multiplying row i by S_i multiplies the determinant by S_i, so det A'_{n,1} equals the resulting triangular product divided by prod_i S_i; that rescaling is never divided out, the case S_i=0 is not addressed, and the assertion that the assignments r_i <- S_i r_i + r_{i-1} (2<=i<=n-1) triangularize the minor - and that the final diagonal entry is exactly the claimed factorization sum - is made with no induction. I verified the mechanism does produce the right answer in the floor(X)=4 cases (n=3 and n=4), and the stated formula is true because beta is the Dirichlet inverse of alpha; so this is an incomplete proof of a true statement rather than a false claim.
0469-0472 'Consider the case of chi an even character': the odd case chi(-1)=-1 is never treated anywhere, so Theorem PreobZZ is at best addressed for even chi. Incompleteness of the proof relative to the stated theorem.
0473-0484 g_chi entire, lambda:=log X-2, r_lambda(H): correct for even chi, since (s-1-beta_0) is cancelled by the real zero and (s+1)(s+3) by the trivial zeros of L at -2,-4.
0485-0491 Mellin formula int_1^inf M_chi(x,y_0)x^{-s}dx = 1/((s-1)L(s-1,chi)) prod_{3<=p<=y_0}(1-chi(p)p^{-(s-1)})^{-1}: verified. int_1^inf A(x)x^{-s}dx=D(s-1)/(s-1) and D(w)=(1-chi(2)2^{-w})prod_{p>y_0}(1-chi(p)p^{-w}) = L(w,chi)^{-1}prod_{3<=p<=y_0}(1-chi(p)p^{-w})^{-1}. Convergence needs Re s>2, as stated.
0492-0501 Interchange of integrals and the resulting integrand: correct; on Re s=3 absolute convergence holds (e^{-t^2/lambda} decay, |t|^{-3} from the denominator), and L(s-1,chi) cancels, leaving prod(...)^{-1}/((s-1-beta_0)(s-1)(s+1)(s+3)).
0502-0515 Residue at s=1+beta_0 and lower bound: correct. Shifting to Re s = 1+beta_0-1/log y_0 stays strictly right of s=1 and of the Euler-product poles, which all lie on Re s=1, so only s=1+beta_0 is crossed; the residue is computed correctly; prod_{3<=p<=y_0}(1-chi(p)p^{-beta_0})^{-1} >> 1/log y_0 by Mertens and e^{(1+beta_0)lambda} asymp X^{1+beta_0}, giving U >> X^{1+beta_0}/log y_0, which dominates the stated error O(X^{1+beta_0-1/log y_0}log y_0). (A harmless sqrt(lambda) from the vertical integral is omitted from the error term.)
0516-0521 Bound |r_lambda(H)| <= e^{-lambda(|H|-1)} for H<=-2 on sigma=lambda: valid. Re(s^2)/lambda = lambda-t^2/lambda, |e^{Hs}|=e^{-|H|lambda}, |g_chi| <= zeta(lambda-1)/((lambda-2)(lambda+1)(lambda+3)) <= 2/(lambda-2), and (1/2pi)sqrt(pi lambda)*2/(lambda-2) <= 1 for lambda large. Crude but correct.
0522-0531 Tail x>=X: correct. X=e^{lambda+2} so H<=-2 there; e^{lambda^2+lambda}[x^{2-lambda}/(2-lambda)] evaluates to e^{lambda+4}/(lambda-2)=e^2 X/(lambda-2) << X.
0532-0540 Shift to sigma=0 and the convexity bound: the shift is legitimate (g_chi entire) and on sigma=0 both |e^{s^2/lambda}|<=1 and |e^{Hs}|=1, giving a bound uniform in H. The functional equation plus Stirling give L(-1+it,chi) << q^{3/2}(|t|+1)^{3/2}, not q^{3/2}|t|^{3/2}: as literally displayed, int |t|^{3/2}/|t|^3 dt diverges at t=0. The stated conclusion |r_lambda(H)| << q^{3/2} is nevertheless correct because the denominator |(s-1-beta_0)(s+1)(s+3)| is bounded away from 0 near t=0. Sloppy display, harmless.
0541-0549 |U| << q^{3/2} int_1^X |M_chi(x,y_0)|dx and the combined inequality X^{1+beta_0}/(q^{3/2}log y_0) << int_1^X|M_chi|: correct; the dropped O(X) tail is absorbed since the lower bound is >> X^{1+beta_0}/log y_0 >> X.
0551-0559 FIRST DECISIVE FAILURE. The estimate |M_chi(x,y_0)| << x exp(-c(log x)^{3/5}(log_2 x)^{-1/5}) for X^c << x << X, with y_0 and q both asymp exp(c(log X)^{2/5}(log_2 X)^{1/5}), is simply asserted 'by an argument similar to that of [Koukoulopoulos]'. No argument is given, the l_0-th-derivative device alluded to at 0268-0270 is never carried out, uniformity in x and the effectivity/independence of the implied constant with respect to chi are never addressed - and effectivity is precisely what is at stake for a Landau-Siegel zero. This asserted bound is exactly the twisted analogue of the 'level' hypothesis that Section 1 concedes is not established, and Section 4 does nothing but convert this bound into a contradiction with a Siegel zero, so the assertion is at least as strong as the theorem it is used to prove. The step is unjustified and the unconditional Theorem PreobZZ is therefore not proved.
0560-0564 Final deduction: the arithmetic is correct GIVEN the asserted bound - int_1^X|M_chi| << X^{2c}+X^2 e^{-c'(log X)^{3/5}(log_2 X)^{-1/5}}, and since (3/2)log q asymp (log X)^{2/5}(log_2 X)^{1/5} = o((log X)^{3/5}(log_2 X)^{-1/5}), one gets (1-beta_0)log X >> (log X)^{3/5}(log_2 X)^{-1/5}, i.e. 1-beta_0 >> (log X)^{-2/5}(log_2 X)^{-1/5} asymp 1/log q. But 'the constant c>0 is effectively computable' is inherited wholesale from the unproved input of 0551-0559, so the conclusion is not established.

Verdict: INVALID. The core results that are actually proved (the inversion formula of Theorem 1, the identity M(X,y)=sum_{floor(X/2)<n<=floor(X)}beta(n,y), the Mertens lemma, and the X=6 numerical example) are all correct, and I verified the X=6 computation and the small-matrix Cramer computations by hand. The failure is that Theorem PreobZZ, stated unconditionally, rests at 0551-0559 on an unproved estimate for M_chi(x,y_0) of exactly the strength being deduced; secondary defects are the false n=1 case of the recursion at 0227, the unaccounted row-scaling factors prod S_i in the Cramer-rule proof at 0458-0467, the missing hypothesis alpha(1)!=0, and the omission of odd characters at 0471.
